spots.name: Aztec sun stone
spots.summary: The Aztec sun stone is a late post-classic Mexica sculpture housed in the National Anthropology Museum in Mexico City, and is perhaps the most famous work of Mexica sculpture. It measures 3.6 metres (12 ft) in diameter and 98 centimetres (39 in) thick, and weighs 24,590 kg (54,210 lb).

spots.name: Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.summary: The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Assumption of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary into Heaven, also commonly called the Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral, is the cathedral church of the Catholic Archdiocese of Mexico.

spots.name: Zócalo
spots.summary: Zócalo is the common name of the main square in central Mexico City. Prior to the conquest by Spain, it was the main ceremonial center in the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan. The plaza used to be known simply as the Plaza Mayor or Plaza de Armas, and today its formal name is Plaza de la Constitución.

spots.name: National Palace
spots.summary: The National Palace is the seat of the federal executive in Mexico. Since 2018 it has also served as the official residence for the President of Mexico. It is located on Mexico City's main square, the Plaza de la Constitución.

spots.name: Historic center of Mexico City
spots.summary: The historic center of Mexico City, also known as the Centro or Centro Histórico, is the central neighborhood in Mexico City, Mexico, focused on the Zócalo and extending in all directions for a number of blocks, with its farthest extent being west to the Alameda Central.

spots.name: Chapultepec Castle
spots.summary: Chapultepec Castle is located on top of Chapultepec Hill in Mexico City's Chapultepec park. The name Chapultepec is the Nahuatl word chapoltepēc which means "on the hill of the grasshopper". It is located at the entrance to Chapultepec park, at a height of 2,325 metres (7,628 ft) above sea level.

spots.name: Torre Latinoamericana
spots.summary: The Torre Latinoamericana is a skyscraper in downtown Mexico City. Its central location, height, and history make it one of the city's most important landmarks.

spots.name: National Museum of Anthropology
spots.summary: The National Museum of Anthropology is a national museum of Mexico. It is the largest and most visited museum in Mexico.

spots.name: Monumento a la Revolución
spots.summary: The Monument to the Revolution is a memorial arch commemorating the Mexican Revolution. It is located in the Plaza de la República, near the heart of the major thoroughfares Paseo de la Reforma and Avenida de los Insurgentes in downtown Mexico City.

spots.name: Angel of Independence
spots.summary: The Angel of Independence, most commonly known by the shortened name El Ángel and officially known as Monumento a la Independencia, is a victory column on a roundabout on the major thoroughfare of Paseo de la Reforma in downtown Mexico City.

spots.name: Chapultepec
spots.summary: Chapultepec, more commonly called the "Bosque de Chapultepec" in Mexico City, is one of the largest city parks in Mexico, measuring in total just over 866 hectares. Centered on a rock formation called Chapultepec Hill, one of the park's main functions is as an ecological space in Greater Mexico City.

spots.name: Paseo de la Reforma
spots.summary: Paseo de la Reforma is a wide avenue that runs diagonally across the heart of Mexico City.

spots.name: Templo Mayor
spots.summary: The Templo Mayor was the main temple of the Mexica people in their capital city of Tenōchtitlan, which is now Mexico City.

spots.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
spots.summary: The Frida Kahlo Museum, also known as The Blue House for the structure's cobalt-blue walls, is a historic house museum and art museum dedicated to the life and work of Mexican artist Frida Kahlo. It is in the Colonia del Carmen neighborhood of Coyoacán in Mexico City.

spots.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
spots.summary: The Palacio de Bellas Artes is a prominent cultural center in Mexico City. It hosts performing arts events, literature events and plastic arts galleries and exhibitions.

spots.name: Ciudad Universitaria
spots.summary: Ciudad Universitaria is the main campus of the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), located in Coyoacán borough in the southern part of Mexico City.

spots.name: Museo Nacional de Arte
spots.summary: The Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) is the Mexican national art museum, located in the historical center of Mexico City. The museum is housed in a neoclassical building at No. 8 Tacuba, Col. Centro, Mexico City.

spots.name: Los Pinos

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Los Pinos was the official residence and office of the President of Mexico from 1934 to 2018. Located in the Bosque de Chapultepec in central Mexico City, it became the presidential seat in 1934, when Gen. Lázaro Cárdenas became the first president to live there.

spots.name: Palacio de Correos de México
spots.summary: The Palacio de Correos de México, also known as the "Correo Mayor" is located in the historic center of Mexico City, on the Eje Central near the Palacio de Bellas Artes. It was built in 1907, when the Post Office became a separate government entity.

spots.name: El Caballito
spots.summary: The equestrian statue of Charles IV of Spain is a bronze sculpture cast by Manuel Tolsá built between 1796 and 1803 in Mexico City, Mexico in honour of King Charles IV of Spain, then the last ruler of the New Spain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Equestrian statue of Charles IV of Spain

spots.name: Colegio de San Ildefonso
spots.summary: Colegio de San Ildefonso, currently is a museum and cultural center in Mexico City, considered to be the birthplace of the Mexican Muralism movement. San Ildefonso began as a prestigious Jesuit boarding school, and after the Reform War it gained educational prestige again as National Preparatory School.

spots.name: Alameda Central
spots.summary: Alameda Central is a public urban park in downtown Mexico City. Established in 1592, Alameda Central is the oldest public park in the Americas. Located in Cuauhtémoc borough between Juárez Avenue and Hidalgo Avenue, the park is adjacent to the Palacio de Bellas Artes and can be accessed by Metro Bellas Artes.

spots.name: Plaza México
spots.summary: The Plaza de toros México, situated in Mexico City, is the world's largest bullring. The 41,262-seat facility is usually dedicated to bullfighting, but many boxing matches have been held there as well, including Julio César Chávez's third and final bout with Frankie Randall on May 22, 2004.

spots.name: Chapultepec Zoo
spots.summary: Chapultepec Zoo is a zoo located in Chapultepec Park; it is one of four zoos near Mexico City, and the best known Mexican zoo.

spots.name: Palace of Iturbide
spots.summary: The Palace of Iturbide is a large palatial residence located in the historic center of Mexico City at Madero Street #17. It was built by the Count of San Mateo Valparaíso as a wedding gift for his daughter.

spots.name: Church of San Francisco

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Convent of San Francisco is located at the western end of Madero Street in the historic center of Mexico City, near the Torre Latinoamericana and is all that remains of the church and monastery complex.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Convent of San Francisco, Madero Street, Mexico City

spots.name: Lake Xochimilco
spots.summary: Lake Xochimilco is an ancient endorheic lake, located in the present-day Borough of Xochimilco in southern Mexico City. It is the last remaining habitat of the axolotl.

spots.name: Torre Mayor

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre Mayor is an office skyscraper in Mexico City, Mexico that is the eighth tallest building in Mexico with a height of 225 meters. From its completion in 2003 until 2010, it was the tallest building in Latin America; it was surpassed by the 236 m (774 ft) high Ocean Two in Panama City, Panama.

spots.name: Academy of San Carlos

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Academy of San Carlos, formerly also known as the National School of Fine Arts, is an art academy in Mexico City that historically played an important role in the development of Mexican art and architecture.

spots.name: Templo Mayor Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This excellent four-story museum was designed by Mexican architect Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, and built in 1987 to showcase the many artifacts found on the site. Highlights include the Coyolxauhqui disc as well as the many thousands of offerings found during the still-ongoing excavation.

spots.name: Franz Mayer Museum
spots.summary: The Franz Mayer Museum, in Mexico City opened in 1986 to house, display and maintain Latin America’s largest collection of decorative arts.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Monument to Cuauhtémoc
spots.summary: The Monument to Cuauhtémoc is an 1887 monument dedicated to the last Mexica ruler (tlatoani) of Tenochtitlan Cuauhtémoc, located at the intersection of Avenida de los Insurgentes and Paseo de la Reforma in Mexico City.

spots.name: Porta Coeli Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Porta Coeli Cathedral also called Church of the Gate of Heaven or Church of Porta Coeli is a cathedral of the Melkite Greek Catholic Church in full communion with the Pope in Rome. It is located in Mexico City, the capital of Mexico.

spots.name: Madero Street
spots.summary: Francisco I. Madero Avenue, commonly known as simply Madero Street, is a geographically and historically significant pedestrian street of Mexico City and a major thoroughfare of the historic city center. It has an east–west orientation from Zócalo to the Eje Central.

spots.name: Museo Nacional de las Culturas
spots.summary: The Museo Nacional de las Culturas is a national museum in Mexico City dedicated to education about the world's cultures, both past and present. It is housed in a colonial-era building that used to be the mint for making coins. Prior to this, the site was the home of the location of the Moctezuma's Black House.

spots.name: Torre Reforma

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre Reforma is an office skyscraper in Mexico City with a height of 807 feet (246 m) to the roof and housing 57 stories.

spots.name: Church of San Felipe Neri "La Profesa"
spots.summary: The Church of San Felipe Neri, commonly known as "La Profesa", is a Roman Catholic parish church that was established by the Society of Jesus late in the 16th century as the church of a community of professed Jesuits.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of San Felipe Neri "La Profesa"

spots.name: Templo Expiatorio Nacional de San Felipe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Templo Expiatorio Nacional de San Felipe de Jesús is an historic church in Mexico City, Mexico.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Templo Expiatorio Nacional de San Felipe de Jesús

spots.name: Museo de Arte Moderno
spots.summary: The Museo de Arte Moderno (MAM) is a museum dedicated to modern Mexican art located in Chapultepec Park in Mexico City.

spots.name: Palacio del Marqués del Apartado
spots.summary: The Palace of the Marquis del Apartado is a historic residence located in Mexico City, just to the northeast of the city's Zocalo in the Historic center of Mexico City.

spots.name: Q8843219
spots.summary: The Estela de Luz is a monument in Mexico City built in 2011 to commemorate the bicentenary of Mexico's independence from Spanish rule. Its design was the winning entry in an invited competition to seek the best combination of Mexico's past and future; the design uses quartz and electric lighting to achieve this effect.

spots.name: Diana the Huntress Fountain
spots.summary: The Huntress Diana Fountain is a sculpture situated within the roundabout at the intersection of Paseo de la Reforma and Río Misisipí and Sevilla streets, on the border of the Colonia Cuauhtémoc and Colonia Juárez neighborhoods in Mexico City.

spots.name: Monument to Christopher Columbus
spots.summary: The Monument to Christopher Columbus is a statue by French sculptor Charles Cordier first dedicated in 1877. It was originally located on a major traffic roundabout along Mexico City's Paseo de la Reforma, and was removed on 10 October 2020 in advance of protests.

spots.name: Museo Nacional de Historia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum of History, also known as MNH, is a national museum of Mexico, located inside Chapultepec Castle in Mexico City. The Castle itself is found within the first section of the well known Chapultepec Park. The museum received 2,135,465 visitors in 2017.

spots.name: Plaza Garibaldi
spots.summary: Plaza Garibaldi is located in monumental downtown, Mexico City, on Eje Central between historic Calle República de Honduras and Calle República de Peru, a few blocks north of the Palacio de Bellas Artes.

spots.name: Museo Nacional de las Intervenciones

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museo Nacional de las Intervenciones is located in the former Monastery of San Diego Churubusco, which was built on top of an Aztec shrine. The museum is split into two sections.

spots.name: Torre BBVA México

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre BBVA México is an office skyscraper on Paseo de la Reforma in Colonia Juárez, Mexico City. It is the headquarters of BBVA México, Mexico's largest bank and a subsidiary of Spanish financial company Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA).

spots.name: Leon Trotsky House Museum
spots.summary: The Leon Trotsky House Museum, Trotsky Museum, or Trotsky House Museum, is a museum honoring Leon Trotsky and an organization that works to promote political asylum, located in the Coyoacán neighborhood of Mexico City. Its official name is Instituto del Derecho de Asilo - Museo Casa de León Trotsky.

spots.name: Palacio de la Autonomía
spots.summary: The Palacio de la Autonomía is a museum and site where the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México gained autonomy from direct government control in 1929.

spots.name: How Doth the Little Crocodile
spots.summary: How Doth the Little Crocodile is both a painting and an outdoor bronze sculpture by British-born Mexican artist Leonora Carrington.

spots.name: Santa Teresa la Antigua

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Teresa la Antigua is a former convent located in the historic center of Mexico City on Licenciado Primo de Verdad #6 just northeast of the city's main plaza. The complex ceased to be a convent in the latter part of the 19th century and has housed the Santa Teresa la Antigua Alternative Art Center since 1989.

spots.name: World Trade Center Mexico City

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The World Trade Center Mexico City, commonly known by its former name, Hotel de México, is a building complex located in the wealthy neighborhood of Colonia Nápoles in central Mexico City.

spots.name: Avenida Juárez
spots.summary: Avenida Juárez is a street in the Historic Center of Mexico City flanking the south side of the centuries-old Alameda Central park.

spots.name: Museo Mural Diego Rivera
spots.summary: Museo Mural Diego Rivera is a museum in Mexico City where Diego Rivera's 1946–47 mural Sueño de una Tarde Dominical en la Alameda Central is located.

spots.name: Benito Juárez Hemicycle
spots.summary: The Benito Juárez Hemicycle is a Neoclassical monument located at the Alameda Central park in Mexico City, Mexico and commemorating the Mexican statesman Benito Juárez. The statue of Juárez is flanked by marble Doric columns. There are two allegorical female statues next to Juárez, representing the fatherland and law.

spots.name: Museo de la Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público
spots.summary: The Museo de la Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público is an art museum located in the historic center of Mexico City. It is housed in what was the Palacio del Arzobispado, built in 1530 under Friar Juan de Zumárraga on the base of the destroyed pyramid dedicated to the Aztec god Tezcatlipoca.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museo de la Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público

spots.name: Jesus Nazareno Church, historic center of Mexico City

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Anahuacalli Museum
spots.summary: The Diego Rivera Anahuacalli Museum is a museum and arts center in Mexico City, located in the San Pablo de Tepetlapa neighborhood of Coyoacán, 10 minutes by car from the Frida Kahlo Museum, as well as from the tourist neighborhood of this district.

spots.name: Luis Barragán House and Studio
spots.summary: Luis Barragán House and Studio, also known as Casa Luis Barragán, is the former residence of architect Luis Barragán in Miguel Hidalgo district, Mexico City. It is owned by the Fundación de Arquitectura Tapatía and the Government of the State of Jalisco.

spots.name: Sagrario Metropolitano
spots.summary: A side chapel next to the Cathedral completed in 1769. The façade is an excellent example of Mexican Churrigueresque architecture.

spots.name: Banco de México
spots.summary: Office of the Mexican Central Bank, built in 1925.

spots.name: Palacio de Minería

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Formerly the Mining College, this building dated from 1792 features an old library and a chapel. It serves as venue for the yearly Mexico City Book Fair.

spots.name: Templo de la Enseñanza
spots.summary: Tucked away on a side street, this very narrow gem of a church was built in the 1770s and is notable for being an outstanding example of Mexican Churrigueresque architecture. Even more remarkable than the façade, however, are the nine gilt retablos inside.

spots.name: Plaza de la Fundación
spots.summary: This place is allegedly where the Aztecs found the eagle eating a snake on top of a cactus (nopal), the divine sign of the gods to settle down and establish the city of Tenochtitlán. It features a sculpture by Juan Olaguibel made in 1970.
